source.title: 日内动量脉冲与股价过度反应的精细刻画
source.note: Original private report is not distributed. Construction is paraphrased and numerical choices are explicitly analyst assumptions.

exposure.reason: Continuation context already contains old EVENT_U results and prior knowledge. This reconstruction re-reads the source; it is not a newly blind trial.
exposure.independent_source_challenger: pfvv_source_challenger: source-only isolated session; not an independent mathematical proof

study_scope.signal_known_at: After the close of the final input day
study_scope.trading_note: Source-comparison monthly diagnostics and Ultimate local-IS execution must be reported separately if the existing evaluator uses a different rebalance/holding rule. Do not compound overlapping 20-day labels as daily returns.
study_scope.warmup: 20 consecutive market trading days; no pre-2016 data assumed; no compressed rolling over missing stock-days

source_native.economic_hypothesis: Intraday relative return bursts and dispersion between volume-defined trading episodes may reflect overreaction; stocks with more stable measured intraday behavior have higher subsequent returns.
pf_steps: Same-minute arithmetic mean of positive and negative stock returns separately
Subtract the same-sign mean, zero return maps to zero deviation
Select minutes with strictly positive cross-sectional skewness of deviations
Sum each stock's log deviation over selected minutes into ONE daily value
Compute 20-day standard deviation of that daily value
vv_steps: Recursively split each stock's remaining volume sequence for six rounds
For length >= 3 choose maximum volume excluding the two endpoints; peak belongs to left segment
Length 2 splits into singleton segments; length 1 stops
Standard deviation across final segment returns gives daily value
Standardize daily value, then compute 20-day standard deviation
source_native.direction: PF, VV and composite are negative factors; smaller raw statistic is preferred
source_native.neutralization: Market-cap and industry neutralization in report's single-factor tests

reconstruction_assumptions.return_definition: Simple close-to-previous-close within day; first minute close/open; no overnight return. Lunch is a trading-clock adjacency.
reconstruction_assumptions.pf_log_deviation_sensitivity: log1p(simple_return) - log1p(same_sign_mean_simple_return), evaluated numerically without selecting by returns
reconstruction_assumptions.pf_skewness: Population central moment m3 / m2**1.5 over finite same-minute deviations; at least 3 finite stocks; zero variance gives skew 0
reconstruction_assumptions.pf_zero_rule: Valid complete day with no selected minutes gives genuine zero; missing observations or invalid log domain are not zeros
reconstruction_assumptions.vv_opening_rule: The explicit remove-first-10 instruction and 230-minute example take precedence over the later 240-minute prose slip
reconstruction_assumptions.vv_validity_domain: Only retained slots are checked; an invalid retained return remains invalid even if caused by the boundary close of a discarded minute
reconstruction_assumptions.vv_peak_tie_break: First internal maximum in chronological trading-clock order
reconstruction_assumptions.vv_segment_return: Compound all simple minute returns in the segment, including its first minute; singleton return is that minute's return, not zero
reconstruction_assumptions.vv_daily_standardization: Same-day equal-weight cross-sectional z-score over valid daily VV values, ddof=1
reconstruction_assumptions.composite_scaling: At each signal date, cross-sectional z-score PF and VV separately on the common finite stock universe, then equal weight; no partial one-component composite
reconstruction_assumptions.output_sign: Preserve nonnegative PF/VV raw values; high-is-preferred scores are negatives of their common-universe z-scores; composite score is their half sum
reconstruction_assumptions.constant_cross_section: With at least two finite identical observations return z=0; fewer than two gives NaN
reconstruction_assumptions.missing_policy: No price/volume forward fill; missing or invalid inputs within a factor's measurement domain invalidate the affected stock-day. A day with unavailable PF cross-sectional gate is not a no-event zero.
reconstruction_assumptions.calculation_universe: Historical SH/SZ input universe, not today's survivors and not the final portfolio. Same-minute benchmark uses observed finite inputs. Trading restrictions are applied by the existing daily execution layer, not an invented minute-state dataset.
reconstruction_assumptions.scope_limit: These explicit choices make a reproducible source reconstruction, not byte-identical author code or a claim that all source ambiguities are solved. No extra winsorization, rank transform or neutralization is hidden inside the raw kernel.

mathematical_mechanism.equation_attribution: Analyst reconstruction of the source-inspired mechanism, not an equation asserted by the report author

primary.object: Transient belief/price-pressure disturbance b and heterogeneity of episode price impacts
primary.mechanism: Observed log price p = latent reference value v + temporary deviation b; b may partially decay after a behavioral/information shock
primary.projection: E[p(t+h)-p(t) | b(t)] = E[v(t+h)-v(t)] - lambda(h)*b(t), with lambda>0 a falsifiable assumption, not an estimated fact
primary.observation_map: PF and VV are source-defined multi-scale dispersion functionals, not direct identification of b; the final rolling standard deviation loses level/sign, requiring an additional empirical link between dispersion and future return
primary.counterparty: Overreacting or heterogeneous short-horizon traders are a source-inspired candidate; their identity, mandatory participation and persistence are not established
identification_gaps: Positive skewness measures asymmetric tails, not the fraction of rising stocks
Low rolling dispersion is not algebraically equivalent to low current overpricing
Volume peaks do not uniquely identify investor emotion

alternative.object: Permanent information arrival and heterogeneous price discovery
alternative.mechanism: Volume bursts and return dispersion may reflect persistent fundamental information rather than temporary pressure
alternative.discriminating_prediction: Non-reversing or continuing post-event returns undermine a pure overreaction interpretation

null_alias.object: Volatility, liquidity, size exposures and missing/stale-price artifacts
null_alias.mechanism: PF/VV can mechanically proxy ordinary risk/liquidity or sparse observation rather than an additional behavioral state
null_alias.discriminating_prediction: Inspect residual association against prespecified controls and compare component/gate/partition ablations on the same sample; disappearance does not alone identify a unique cause

mathematical_mechanism.knowledge_role: Later references can suggest tests and alternatives; they cannot replace this source baseline

deterministic_checks_before_performance: Independent hand oracle for sign means, deviations, skew gate and daily sum
Counterexample: std(up_daily+down_daily) differs from separate rolling std aggregation
Volume partition covers every retained minute exactly once, peak-left and singleton rules
Singleton segment return is nonzero when its minute return is nonzero
Future-day mutation leaves earlier daily and rolling output unchanged
Missing stock-day occupies its calendar slot; it is not removed from the 20-day window
Valid no-event zero distinguished from missing or invalid input
Composite equal weights apply to explicitly standardized common-universe components
Numerical sensitivity records both log-deviation conventions without return-based choice
